# 妙法蓮華經玄贊

**ID:** T1723
**Volume:** T34
**Category:** 法華部類
**Original Category:** 經疏部
**Byline:** 唐 窺基撰
**Dynasty:** 唐
**Date:** 632–682
**Juans:** 10
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/T1723

## Contributors
- 窺基 (A001019)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A ten-*juan* major doctrinal commentary on the Lotus Sūtra by Kuī-jī 窺基 (632–682), the founding patriarch of the Chinese Yogācāra (Cí'ēn / Fǎxiàng 慈恩 / 法相) school and the principal direct disciple of Xuánzàng 玄奘 (602–664). The work is the most important pre-modern Chinese Yogācāra-school commentary on the Lotus Sūtra and provides the principal scholastic alternative to both the Tiāntái interpretation of Zhìyǐ ([KR6d0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0006) and [KR6d0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0014)) and the Sānlùn interpretation of Jízàng ([KR6d0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0023)–[KR6d0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0025)). The body attribution: *Dà Cí'ēnsì shāmén Jī zhuàn* 大慈恩寺沙門基撰 ("composed by the *śramaṇa* Jī of the Great Cí'ēn Monastery").

**Abstract**

The *Xuánzàn* applies Kuī-jī's distinctive Cí'ēn Yogācāra hermeneutic to the Lotus Sūtra: the *ālayavijñāna* 阿賴耶識 (storehouse-consciousness) doctrine, the *trisvabhāva* 三性 (three-natures: parikalpita / paratantra / pariniṣpanna) classification, the *trinaiḥsvabhāvatā* 三無性 (three non-natures), and the *pañcajñāna* 五智 (five wisdoms) of the *Mahāyānasaṃgraha* and the *Yogācārabhūmi*. Kuī-jī's most distinctive Yogācāra reading of the Lotus is his interpretation of the *ekayāna* (一乘) doctrine through the Yogācāra *gotra* (種姓) theory: the Lotus's claim that all beings will eventually attain Buddhahood is read by Kuī-jī as applying only to the *bodhisattva-gotra* and the *aniyatagotra* (indeterminate-lineage) beings, not to the *pratyekabuddha-gotra* and the *śrāvaka-gotra* — let alone to the *agotra-icchantika* 一闡提 (lineageless ones). This reading directly contradicts the Tiāntái interpretation of the Lotus (which holds that all beings without exception attain Buddhahood) and the Sānlùn interpretation (which dissolves the question through the two-truths framework), and was a major point of polemical contention in seventh- and eighth-century Chinese Buddhism.

The work is consequently of substantial historical importance both as a doctrinal monument and as a record of the intellectual tensions between the major Sino-Buddhist schools at the height of the Táng. It generated a substantial subcommentarial tradition: Huìzhāo's *Fǎhuá xuánzàn yìjué* ([KR6d0027](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0027), T1724); Zhìzhōu's *Fǎhuá jīng xuánzàn shèshì* ([KR6d0028](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0028), X29n0596 — incorrectly catalogued as X34n0636); and Chóngjùn's *Fǎhuá jīng xuánzàn juézé jì* ([KR6d0029](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0029), X34n0637).

The composition is generally dated to Kuījī's mature productive period at the Cí'ēnsì 慈恩寺 in Cháng'ān, c. 660–682. The work was carried to Japan with Xuánzàng's larger Yogācāra corpus and became one of the foundational texts of the Japanese Hossō 法相 school of Nara Buddhism.
